m.title: Market
m.lead: Honesty is stronger than power, but the market is stronger than honesty. So we don't sell the philosophy — we sell services that prove it works.

layers.proves: Proves that reputation is earned through work and cannot be bought.

why: Most projects like this start with a charter and votes, and end with an empty website. We do the opposite: real economic activity first, rules second.
Governance appears when there is something to divide — not before. Once experts have reason to argue about money and access, the charter stops being text and becomes necessary.
Every commercial layer stands on the same core: a verified human, non-transferable reputation, open rules. Different products, one foundation.
m.honest: Live today: signing the charter and questions to humanity. Verified Talent is in development. Wiki and Feed are plans, not promises. There is no token, no token sale is planned, and we make no promises of income.
m.ctaNote: Commercial products live on separate domains — no charter, no ideology there, just the service.

g.title: Shield
g.lead: Your profile here is not a form — it is a shield. It is assembled from parts, and each part proves something different. None of them can be bought.
g.capEmpty: An empty shield. The first part appears the moment you sign.

parts.name: Core
parts.proves: You signed the Constitution — the point everything else starts from.
parts.how: Sign. Half a minute, no account and no email.
parts.gives: A signature number that stays yours permanently.

parts.name: Flag
parts.proves: Your voice counts for your country.
parts.how: Pick your country when signing. Anonymous signers pick it like everyone else — hiding your name does not mean giving up your country.
parts.gives: A count for your country, and for the first hundred there, founder status forever.

parts.name: Frame
parts.proves: You are one person, not ten accounts.
parts.how: Verify personhood. One anchor lets you sign; two independent anchors plus a liveness check let you vote.
parts.gives: Full voting weight. Without the frame a vote does not count — otherwise fake accounts decide everything.

parts.name: Chevrons
parts.proves: You did something and it was checked. Outcome, not activity.
parts.how: Claim a deed and let it be verified: a bot checks what is machine-checkable, the crowd confirms by staking their own karma, a human panel handles what is contested.
parts.gives: Karma. Three chevrons for three levels of verification — the higher the level, the brighter the stripe and the harder it is to dispute.

parts.name: Visor
parts.proves: You stand behind your words with your name.
parts.how: Reveal your name. Voluntary, and it only moves one way — what is revealed cannot be hidden again.
parts.gives: A karma premium for being public. A closed visor carries no penalty: anonymity costs you the premium, never your vote or your rights.

parts.name: Seal
parts.proves: Your qualification is backed by a checkable fact, not a claim.
parts.how: Guild verification. What gets confirmed is narrow — 'licence No. X exists and belongs to this person' — not 'this person is a good professional'.
parts.gives: A say in governing your own field. Doctors decide on medicine, engineers on engineering.

g.rule: No part can be bought, transferred or gifted — only earned. A bot may add a part; only a human or a vote may take one away. A robot's mistake must never cost a person their reputation.
g.karmaT: How the shield relates to karma
karma: Karma is a number. The shield is its shape. Same thing — the system reads the number, people read the shield.
Karma grows for verified outcomes, not for presence. Ten comments change nothing. One confirmed deed adds a stripe.
So a shield cannot be built quickly, and it cannot be built alone: almost every part requires someone else to confirm you.
g.pathT: What opens as it comes together

path.d: Signed. You are on the list, you have a number, and your country counts you as its own.
A vote. Your voice on questions to humanity weighs exactly as much as anyone else's.
Weight in a subject. Your deeds are visible and your opinion in a field you know gets cited.
Governance. You join the circle that sets the rules in your own field.
Your name. You answer publicly — the most expensive part of the shield, because it cannot be undone.

token: In the protocol, karma is a non-transferable record: it cannot be sold along with an account, because it is not about the account — it is about the person.

Later a second, ordinary and liquid unit will sit next to it, paying for the work of the network and for services inside it. The split is the whole point: the liquid thing can be bought, power cannot. Someone with money can pay for any number of operations and still not gain a single extra vote.

None of this exists yet, and it will not for a while. We set ourselves two conditions: ten paying customers and two years of work. A project that issues a token before it has a product collects speculators and regulators instead of participants — and we have seen enough of those to not repeat it.
g.tokenNote: There is no token. No token sale is planned. We make no promises of income, and the shield is status and rights — not a financial instrument.
g.ctaNote: A shield takes years to build and outlives the project: it belongs to the person, not to the website.

const.title: The World Constitution
const.p1: We, the people of Earth, recognise that existing institutions fail to protect the human being and future generations. For the first time in history, technology allows us to fix this: to prove that a person is real and unique without revealing their identity; to give everyone a vote that cannot be forged; and a reputation that cannot be bought or taken away.
const.p2: This document is a living social contract: a voluntary charter striving for universality. It is not a declaration of intent but working code. We do not overthrow the old world by force — we lay a layer of light and trust on top of it and win because life inside it is better.

articles.b: The dignity, life, freedom and safety of every person are inalienable. The rights of future generations are protected equally with those of the present. This article cannot be repealed by any majority — it stands above any vote.

Aggression against one is a threat to all. Aggression is established by transparent verification within 48 hours, not years of debate. This is not a right to vigilante justice: the system creates pressure through light, it does not replace lawful bodies by force.

Falsification becomes technically impossible: every vote is verifiable, yet secrecy is preserved. You cannot prove to a third party how you voted — which kills vote-buying. Re-voting is allowed: a vote cast under pressure can be secretly changed.

The higher the office, the more transparent its holder's finances and decisions must be. The light points upward at power, not downward at the individual. An ordinary person discloses only what they consent to.

No one may control courts, media and elections at the same time. Those who frame questions, judge disputes and count votes are different, replaceable roles. The same holds inside the platform: no permanent moderators, no sole owner of the treasury.

A leader who hands over power voluntarily and peacefully receives recognition and protection rather than persecution. Holding power by force leads to an ethical penalty. This is recognition, not legal immunity: the gravest crimes are excluded.

Decisions are made without anyone holding a veto. Bicameralism — agreement of both people and communities — protects the small from the large. Local matters stay local; only the truly global is decided globally.

Everyone has the right to know how the algorithms shaping their life work: ranking and scoring rules are public. State control over media is forbidden. Algorithmic openness never means exposing people's private lives.

The natural foundations of life are the common heritage of humanity and future generations. Access to them is a right; their stewardship is subject to transparent collective control. Appropriation to the detriment of all is inadmissible.

Trust belongs to the person: it cannot be bought, sold or transferred. It is built from verifiable deeds and assessed by transparent rules, not by a superior's decision. Money does not convert into influence.

articles.t: The platform as a living model
articles.b: The platform itself is a working model of this Constitution. Every principle has a technical embodiment: if a rule does not work in code, it does not work at all. Complexity is added only when it has been earned.

Change is possible, but neither fast nor secret: 80% agreement, mandatory citizen participation and at least six months of deliberation. Any participant may propose an amendment. Article 0 is not subject to amendment.

Violations are recorded transparently; punishment is proportionate and predictable. An ethical penalty follows only from narrow, verifiable events confirmed by several independent sources, with the right of appeal. Sanctions and ICC charges remain visible in any privacy mode.

articles.t: Digital passport and freedom of movement
articles.b: A single trust passport is recognised across borders; movement is a right, not a privilege. Disclosure is by consent and minimal: you prove “verified”, not your whole record. No enumerable registry of people exists.

articles.t: Common heritage of knowledge and authorship
articles.b: Knowledge is a common heritage, yet authorship is respected and protected. The creator receives recognition and royalties; humanity receives access. Protection of authorship never becomes a permanent monopoly on knowledge.

Every request for your data is visible to you: who, when and why. Disclosure happens only with your cryptographic consent. There is no back door for states or for the operator — a hidden social credit score cannot be built.
Animals, plants and ecosystems are not property but living participants of this planet. We are stewards, not owners. Destroying the living world for short-term gain is a violation.

Climate, pandemics and uncontrolled technologies concern everyone and know no borders. The response is collective, transparent and based on verifiable facts. A common threat can never serve as a pretext for suspending rights.

The new system neither overthrows the old by force nor compels anyone — it wins because life inside it is better. Transitional amnesty: reputational forgiveness in exchange for full disclosure of the truth and an end to harm, with a window that narrows over time. This is not legal immunity; the gravest crimes are excluded.

Those not yet born have a representative: an elected role mandated to assess decisions by their long-term consequences. They may demand such an assessment on any question, and their opinion is public. The rights of future generations stop being a declaration and gain a bearer.

k.title: Karma
k.sub: Karma is an open record of what you have done for the common cause. It cannot be bought, transferred or gifted — only earned through deeds.
k.battT: The battery: where you are now
k.battLead: Karma is a number, and one number tells you nothing. So it is shown as a battery: five cells, each charged by a different kind of proof. Charge accumulates and never drops on its own — a cell can only be removed by a human or a vote, through a transparent procedure and with a right of appeal.

segs.name: Signature
segs.need: Sign the Constitution. Half a minute, no account.
segs.opens: your signature number and a count for your country

segs.name: Personhood
segs.need: Prove you are one person: one anchor lets you sign, two independent anchors plus a liveness check let you vote.

segs.name: Deed
segs.need: Claim what you did and let it be verified: a bot, the crowd staking their own karma, or a human panel.
segs.opens: weight in a subject — your opinion gets cited

segs.name: Independence
segs.need: Your deeds are confirmed by people from different clusters, countries and organisations — not only your own circle.

segs.name: Guild
segs.need: Professional verification: a narrow checkable fact is confirmed, never a general endorsement.
segs.opens: a say in the rules of your own field

k.glow: The battery does not drain because you were away. Punishing absence pushes out people with jobs, children or bad internet and keeps only the most unencumbered — which is not fairness. Separate from charge there is a glow: it shows whether you are active right now, fades on its own and lights up with any verified deed. It has no effect on karma or rights at all — only on whether you get invited to panels that need someone who will actually respond this week.

build.d: The basic contribution: you declare that you share these principles. It gives you a signature number that is yours forever.
You set the agenda for humanity. Karma grows more when a question gains support — the result matters, not the act of submitting.
You help surface what matters from the common stream.
The network grows through you. Those who actually take part are counted, not empty sign-ups.
A public profile earns a premium: you stand behind your words with your name. Anonymity is never penalised — it simply carries no premium.
Professionals verify professionals within guilds. The weightiest contribution — and the greatest responsibility.

check.d: A bot checks what a machine can check: signatures, support, a link to your work, a commit, a publication, a referral chain. Instantly, without queues.
What a bot cannot confirm is confirmed by other participants, who stake their own karma: confirm a lie and you lose yours.
Significant, disputed and qualitative matters are decided by humans — as on Wikipedia, but with rotation, recall and appeal by lot. AI never issues a final verdict about a person.

money: Today karma pays nothing — and that is deliberate. Paying for clicks attracts mercenaries and bots, not people.

Karma is recorded in an open contribution ledger. When the protocol starts earning (verifying people for services, professional confirmations), part of the revenue is intended to be distributed retroactively — according to contributions made earlier.
The logic is simple: those who did the work when nothing was paid stand first in line once money appears.
What already earns directly: if an external service requests confirmation of your status, half of the fee goes to you. Only with your consent, for each request separately.
k.warn: The rules of any future distribution will be set by the community, not by us. No guarantees, no promises of income, price or timing are given, and karma is not a financial instrument. If someone promises you income for participating — that is not us.
k.cantT: What cannot be done with karma
cant: Buy it — neither with money nor with tokens
Transfer or gift it to another person
Earn it through empty activity: a verified result is what counts
Take it away arbitrarily — only through a transparent procedure with the right of appeal

q.title: Questions to humanity
q.sub: The agenda is set by people, not by an editorial board. Propose a question humanity should answer — the strongest become global votes.
q.hint: Phrase it neutrally so it can be answered “yes” or “no”. Your question appears in the shared list immediately.
q.label: Question
q.ph: For example: Should social media algorithms be open to independent audit?
q.ok: Question published and recorded in the contribution ledger — it is already in the list below.
q.short: The question is too short — at least 10 characters.
q.empty: No questions yet — propose the first one.
q.loadErr: Could not load the list. Please refresh.
q.ledger: Every proposed and supported question is recorded in an open contribution ledger. Contributions may be taken into account in future retroactive rounds — the rules are defined later and by the community; no guarantees, no promises of income or price are given. Full personal accounting arrives with verification (Stage 1) — for now counters are stored in your browser.

v.bannerTxt: — this is how voting will look. For now it is a mock-up: voting opens after verification.
v.question: Should social media algorithms be open to independent audit?
v.sub: A global question · one verified person = one vote
v.hint: Pick an option to see the result (demo)
v.protect: you cannot prove to a third party how you voted (protection against vote-buying). You may re-vote — the last one counts.
v.mapNote: Demo data for the preview. In the live version — an interactive world map in real time.
v.d1: Algorithmic openness is the only way to check whether the feed is being manipulated. An audit does not mean disclosing personal data.
v.d2: It matters who runs the audit. An independent body is needed, otherwise the audit becomes a formality.
v.d3: Technically feasible: the ranking logic is published, not private data. Working approaches already exist.
v.discNote: The weight of an argument depends on the author's trust — but this does not affect the vote: 1 person = 1 vote.
v.howT: Who creates the questions and who moderates?
v.h1: Participants propose (any verified person), not moderators from above.
v.h2: An AI filter removes spam, duplicates, non-neutral wording and manipulation.
v.h3: The community raises what matters (weight by trust).
v.h4: Stewards (elected, replaceable, public) review only the disputed cases. AI never delivers a final verdict about a person.
v.hFoot: Stewards are moderated mutually: transparency, rotation, recall, appeal by lot, reputation at stake. No one holds final, irremovable power.
